issues.item: Checking Behind: I frequently look behind me to check if someone is following me
issues.explanation: The threat items 'Checking Behind' and 'Back to Wall' imply a persistent interpersonal pursuit/assault-style danger (someone following me, needing surveillance of the room) that is hard to reconcile with a life-threatening motor vehicle collision unless there is additional trauma content not represented elsewhere in the profile.

issues.item: Back to Wall: I feel unsafe unless my back is against a wall where I can see the room
issues.explanation: 'Institutional Failure' is not a natural fit with the rest of this MVC profile: the other items center on fragmented accident memory, mistrust of self/body, and hypervigilance, but this appraisal presupposes a salient protector/institution betrayal theme that is not supported by the trauma type or other selected items.

issues.item: Institutional Failure: The people or institutions that should have protected me let me down
issues.explanation: 'Avoid Social Contacts: Seeing people that I socialised with before the event' does not connect well to the represented triggers, memory, or appraisals. For an MVC case, avoidance is more coherently focused on travel, roads, vehicles, reminders of the crash, or internal trauma cues; avoidance of prior social contacts suggests a different maintaining process that is not otherwise represented.

vignette: Kofi had always been a man who moved with purpose, his long legs eating up the distance as he danced across the stage. But that was before the accident, before the sound of screeching tires and crunching metal became etched in his mind like a scar. It had been two years since the motor vehicle collision that nearly took his life, but for Kofi, time seemed to have frozen. As he lay in the hospital bed, Kofi couldn't shake the feeling that something was off. He remembered fragments of the accident - the smell of smoke, the sound of sirens - but the rest was a jumbled mess. He tried to piece together what had happened, but his mind felt like a puzzle with missing pieces. This sense of incompleteness only added to his growing unease; he couldn't trust that he would ever be able to recall the truth. As Kofi began to recover physically, he found himself increasingly withdrawn. He stopped going out, afraid of being in public spaces where anything could happen. He avoided seeing people he had socialized with before the accident, unable to bear their questions or sympathetic gazes. Even thinking about the therapy sessions he knew he needed felt like too much; he couldn't bring himself to confront the memories that lingered just beneath the surface. Kofi's self-doubt had taken root early on. He questioned whether he would ever be able to trust his body again, whether he was truly safe even in his own home. The people and institutions that were supposed to protect him - the police, the hospital staff - seemed to have failed him, leaving him feeling vulnerable and alone. As a result, Kofi became hyper-vigilant, always on the lookout for potential threats. He felt safest with his back against a wall, where he could see everything happening around him. Delays or unexpected noises sent his heart racing; he was convinced that something bad was lurking just out of sight. Kofi's memories of the accident remained frustratingly incomplete, and this only added to his sense of unease. He felt like he was stuck in a never-ending loop, unable to move forward because he couldn't shake the feeling that he was missing something crucial. This uncertainty fueled his negative appraisals - he couldn't trust himself or anyone else. As Kofi struggled to come to terms with what had happened, his avoidance behaviors became more entrenched. He stopped dancing altogether, afraid of putting himself in a situation where he might get hurt again. His isolation deepened; he barely left the house, unable to bear the thought of facing the world outside. It was only when Kofi's granddaughter began to ask why "Papa" wasn't coming to visit anymore that he realized how much his life had shrunk. He knew he needed help, but the thought of seeking therapy filled him with dread - what if they uncovered memories he couldn't handle? What if he wasn't strong enough to face the truth? Kofi's story is one of a man trapped in a cycle of fear and self-doubt, unable to escape the shadow of his traumatic experience. His maladaptive strategies have become a way of life, but at what cost? As he sits in his darkened living room, surrounded by memories of a life once lived, Kofi wonders if it's too late to find a way back to the light.
